exposure: Newborn status at birth (crying or not crying)
cohort: 1827 newborns taken to the resuscitation table at a tertiary hospital in Nepal
finding: The study found that suction was used in almost 90% of newborns brought to the resuscitation table, while bag-and-mask ventilation was only used in less than 10%, indicating inadequate adherence to neonatal resuscitation guidelines.
mod_finding: Babies delivered by caesarean section were more likely to receive ventilation with bag-and-mask if they were not crying when brought to the resuscitation table (AdjOR 1.64).
birth_weight: Low birth weight babies were more likely to receive bag-and-mask ventilation if they were not crying when brought to the resuscitation table (AdjOR 1.68).
